title: The README quickstart followed as a stranger would, on a fresh clone of the public repository, and both submission issues' benchmark commands against that server
hardware: 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (96 GB), a rented VM

model.checkpoint: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (the hub id, as the README gives it)

steps.uv sync --extra serve --frozen: exit 0 in 66 s (vLLM 0.30.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA available); uv's cache held 0.9 GB from earlier work on this VM, and the remaining 7.4 GB downloaded at full speed, not at the 0.7 MB/s the hand-over expected, so the pre-built image was not needed
steps.server command: uv run python -m decisio.serve.vllm_engine --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --model-class hidden-readout, verbatim, with HF_HOME pointed at a fresh directory: /health answered after 657 s, which includes downloading the 35 GB checkpoint (weights loaded after 353 s, engine initialised in 263 s); the single-engine head loaded the output layer from the hub id (server_start.log)
steps.Ask a question (curl): 200; choices access and level 2 as the README shows; probabilities differ from the README's (readme_curl_responses.json)
steps.Register a task (curl): 200 in 13.6 s for 120 examples; calibration declined (no clear gain), head applied (task_registration_response.json); a question then carried x-decisio-tasks: ticket-routing
steps.examples/tasks/evaluate.py: accuracy before 1.000, after 1.000 on the 48 held-out tickets: the served model already routes the synthetic tickets correctly (walkthrough_evaluate.txt)

deviations: README: the abridged example response lists different probabilities than this server returned (access 0.79 in the README, 0.872 here; 0.906 on one request after the benchmark stage); the README does not say that the values move with request history. Fixed in the same pull request.

JevBench issue (fstandhartinger/jevbench#169): its harness command ends in '...' and fails as written ('the following arguments are required: --results'); the complete form is benchmarks/jevbench.sh, which ran without change. Corrected in a comment on the issue.

Decision Index issue (apolinario/decision-index#38): `python -m decision_index pipeline ...` as written fails for anyone but the kit's operator, because the frozen suite dataset is private (401; the kit's issue #1). Ran instead benchmarks/decision_index.sh on the kit's own four-benchmark rebuild (the rows' sha256 equals the records'). Stated in a comment on the issue.
Operator steps not in the README and not decisio defects: HF_HOME was set by us; the VM's uv cache was not empty.

jevbench.against_runs/2026-09-30_served-default: 231 of 231 predictions the same; probabilities within 2.2e-16

decision_index.against_runs/2026-09-30_served-default: 20,810 of 20,810 requests with the same choices and payload sha256; probabilities within 3.3e-16 on all but 2 MMLU-Pro requests (up to 0.078, request history)

files.jevbench/<file>/: the harness's results.jsonl, summary.json, manifest.json; v15.json
files.decision_index/: per request: ids, the payload's sha256, our response (no payload); the kit's summary, our report and calibration
